use_cases.title: Onboarding material
use_cases.detail: Generate explainers for new team members instead of writing docs from scratch.

pros: Explanations are video, not a chat transcript
Follow-up questions keep the context
Public examples let you judge quality first
cons: Pricing is not published
Video generation is slower than reading an answer

name: Smart Blur
description: Smart Blur is a Chrome extension that blurs personal data on screen shares and screenshots. Emails, phone numbers and card numbers blur on any page as it loads, and anything else takes a click. Everything runs on your device with no account, and the Pro version switches itself on the moment a screen share starts.
description_en: Smart Blur is a Chrome extension that blurs personal data on screen shares and screenshots. Emails, phone numbers and card numbers blur on any page as it loads, and anything else takes a click. Everything runs on your device with no account, and the Pro version switches itself on the moment a screen share starts.
best_for: People who demo or present from a live browser
Support staff sharing screens with customers

use_cases.title: Safe screen sharing
use_cases.detail: Blur emails, phone numbers and card numbers before anyone sees your screen.

use_cases.title: Screenshot redaction
use_cases.detail: Clean a capture of personal data without opening an image editor.

use_cases.title: Automatic mode
use_cases.detail: With Pro, blurring turns on as soon as a share starts.

pros: Runs on device, no account needed
Blurs automatically as pages load
Free tier covers the common cases
cons: Automatic screen-share detection is Pro only
Chrome only

name: Ekselio
description: Ekselio by GPTBeyond is an AI-native office of the CFO: an AI designs the workflow and a deterministic engine executes it, producing auditable SQL and Excel models with Power Query that recompute and verify their own numbers. Connect QuickBooks Online or drop any export; your files are never uploaded because every step runs in your browser.
description_en: Ekselio by GPTBeyond is an AI-native office of the CFO: an AI designs the workflow and a deterministic engine executes it, producing auditable SQL and Excel models with Power Query that recompute and verify their own numbers. Connect QuickBooks Online or drop any export; your files are never uploaded because every step runs in your browser.
best_for: Finance teams that need auditable analysis
CFOs who do not want their books in a model provider

use_cases.title: Auditable finance workflows
use_cases.detail: Get analysis whose every step is inspectable as SQL.

use_cases.title: Excel-verifiable models
use_cases.detail: Export a model that recomputes and checks its own numbers.

use_cases.title: QuickBooks reporting
use_cases.detail: Connect QuickBooks Online or drop an export and describe the analysis you need.

pros: Deterministic execution rather than a generated guess
Runs in the browser, files are not uploaded
Exports to Excel with Power Query
cons: Pricing is not published
Oriented around QuickBooks workflows

name: 0sql
description: 0sql is an open source semantic layer that returns SQL rather than answering questions itself. You model your warehouse in YAML, post a query spec in business terms, and get back one correct, deterministic SQL statement or a refusal that explains why. It never connects to your warehouse and never runs a query.
description_en: 0sql is an open source semantic layer that returns SQL rather than answering questions itself. You model your warehouse in YAML, post a query spec in business terms, and get back one correct, deterministic SQL statement or a refusal that explains why. It never connects to your warehouse and never runs a query.
best_for: Teams that do not want a model writing SQL
Data platform groups defining metrics once
Anyone burned by a plausible wrong query

use_cases.title: Metric definitions in YAML
use_cases.detail: Model the warehouse once and let every consumer share the definition.

use_cases.title: Deterministic SQL generation
use_cases.detail: Post business terms and receive one SQL statement you can read.

use_cases.title: Safe refusals
use_cases.detail: Get an explanation instead of SQL when the request cannot be answered from the model.

pros: Never touches your warehouse or runs queries
Refuses with a reason instead of guessing
MIT licensed
cons: Requires modelling your warehouse in YAML first
Self-hosting and ops are on you

name: RooQL
description: RooQL is an open source semantic layer built on Apache Ossie that ships inside your app rather than as a separate service. Define every metric once and give every Claude artifact one source of truth, with zero infrastructure. A browser playground lets you try it without signing up.
description_en: RooQL is an open source semantic layer built on Apache Ossie that ships inside your app rather than as a separate service. Define every metric once and give every Claude artifact one source of truth, with zero infrastructure. A browser playground lets you try it without signing up.
best_for: Teams giving agents a consistent metric definition
Apps that cannot run another service
Developers embedding a semantic layer in a product

use_cases.title: One source of truth for metrics
use_cases.detail: Define a metric once and let every generated artifact use it.

use_cases.title: In-app semantic layer
use_cases.detail: Ship the layer with your app instead of hosting a separate service.

use_cases.title: Try before installing
use_cases.detail: Ask questions in the browser playground without an account.

pros: No infrastructure to operate
Apache 2.0 licensed
Browser playground for evaluation
cons: Tied to Apache Ossie
Young project

name: OpenHand Sidekick
description: Sidekick by OpenHand is an AI companion for telehealth visits. It joins the visit in real time, explains medical terms as they come up and suggests questions worth asking, so patients leave understanding what was said.
description_en: Sidekick by OpenHand is an AI companion for telehealth visits. It joins the visit in real time, explains medical terms as they come up and suggests questions worth asking, so patients leave understanding what was said.
best_for: Patients who leave appointments with unanswered questions
Caregivers joining on someone else's behalf
Anyone who wants jargon translated live

use_cases.title: Live terminology help
use_cases.detail: Get medical terms explained while the appointment is still running.

use_cases.title: Question prompts
use_cases.detail: Receive suggested questions so nothing important goes unasked.

use_cases.title: Post-visit recall
use_cases.detail: Leave with a clearer record of what was discussed.

pros: Works during the visit rather than after it
Explains terms and prompts questions
Simple patient-facing framing
cons: Limited early access at launch
Health context means extra care about accuracy

name: Rgpu
description: Rgpu lets you keep Python on your laptop while running PyTorch operations and holding tensors on a remote GPU. It works from a Mac with no CUDA installation, so training and experiment code stays local while the compute happens elsewhere.
description_en: Rgpu lets you keep Python on your laptop while running PyTorch operations and holding tensors on a remote GPU. It works from a Mac with no CUDA installation, so training and experiment code stays local while the compute happens elsewhere.
best_for: Developers on laptops without a usable GPU
Mac users who cannot install CUDA
Teams sharing one remote machine for experiments

use_cases.title: Remote tensors from a Mac
use_cases.detail: Hold tensors on a remote GPU while your code runs locally.

use_cases.title: Keeping the local workflow
use_cases.detail: Avoid rewriting scripts for a remote environment.

use_cases.title: Sharing one GPU box
use_cases.detail: Point several laptops at a single machine with the accelerators.

pros: No CUDA install needed on the client
Keeps the Python workflow on your own machine
Open source
cons: Requires a remote GPU you control
C++ extension and network setup to install

name: ForgeMesh
description: ForgeMesh Labs runs paid APIs aimed at AI agents: notarization, anomaly detection, disruption intel, travel, voice, market signals and image generation. Agents pay per call over x402 or MPP with no accounts and no API keys, and the catalogue is also exposed as MCP servers.
description_en: ForgeMesh Labs runs paid APIs aimed at AI agents: notarization, anomaly detection, disruption intel, travel, voice, market signals and image generation. Agents pay per call over x402 or MPP with no accounts and no API keys, and the catalogue is also exposed as MCP servers.
best_for: Agents that need to buy a service without human signup
Teams avoiding per-vendor API key management

use_cases.title: Per-call paid services
use_cases.detail: Let an agent pay for a single call instead of holding a subscription.

use_cases.title: Key-free integration
use_cases.detail: Access services over x402 or MPP without provisioning credentials.

use_cases.title: MCP access
use_cases.detail: Expose the same catalogue to agents through MCP servers.

pros: No accounts or API keys to manage
Pay-per-call pricing model
MCP servers available
cons: Depends on x402 or MPP payment rails
Pay-per-call costs need monitoring in an agent loop

name: Titan
description: Titan is a desktop AI assistant that sees what is on your screen and does the work in the apps you already use. You say what you want, it works the apps you already pay for, and it remembers what you tell it. The site says it is free to download.
description_en: Titan is a desktop AI assistant that sees what is on your screen and does the work in the apps you already use. You say what you want, it works the apps you already pay for, and it remembers what you tell it. The site says it is free to download.
best_for: Users who want an assistant over existing desktop apps
People tired of AI that only lives in a browser tab
Anyone who wants an assistant that remembers context

use_cases.title: Working the apps you have
use_cases.detail: Ask for a task in an app you already use instead of switching to a chat window.

use_cases.title: Screen-aware help
use_cases.detail: Let the assistant see what you are looking at when you ask.

use_cases.title: Persistent context
use_cases.detail: Have it remember what you told it across sessions.

pros: Operates on your screen rather than in a tab
Free to download at launch
Aims at apps you already pay for
cons: Screen access raises obvious privacy questions
New product with little track record

name: Pi Codex Connectors
description: Pi Codex Connectors is a Pi extension that lets any Pi model use your connected Codex apps and direct web search. It starts codex app-server on first use, with Codex keeping ownership of your login and connector credentials, and exposes three tools instead of hundreds of schemas.
description_en: Pi Codex Connectors is a Pi extension that lets any Pi model use your connected Codex apps and direct web search. It starts codex app-server on first use, with Codex keeping ownership of your login and connector credentials, and exposes three tools instead of hundreds of schemas.
best_for: Pi users with Codex connectors configured
Developers who want connector access from any model
Anyone avoiding giant tool schemas in context

use_cases.title: Connector access from Pi
use_cases.detail: Call your connected Codex apps from a non-Codex model.

use_cases.title: Compact tool catalogue
use_cases.detail: Use three tools to list, inspect and call connectors instead of loading every schema.

use_cases.title: Direct web search
use_cases.detail: Search and read the public web through the standalone search endpoint.

pros: Keeps credentials with Codex, not the extension
Three tools instead of hundreds of schemas
Works with any Pi model
cons: Requires a Codex login and Pi setup
Backend behaviour of the search endpoint is not fully documented

name: Experiential
description: Experiential is an open source gateway and router for agent workflows. It puts hosted, bring-your-own-key and local models behind one OpenAI-compatible API, controls which users and agents can use which models and how much they can spend, and turns production traffic into a custom router or model tuned for quality, speed and cost.
description_en: Experiential is an open source gateway and router for agent workflows. It puts hosted, bring-your-own-key and local models behind one OpenAI-compatible API, controls which users and agents can use which models and how much they can spend, and turns production traffic into a custom router or model tuned for quality, speed and cost.

use_cases.title: One API for every model
use_cases.detail: Call hosted, bring-your-own-key and local models through a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint instead of wiring each provider separately.

use_cases.title: Budgets per agent
use_cases.detail: Decide which users and agents may use which models, for which use cases, and cap how much each of them can spend.

use_cases.title: A router learned from your traffic
use_cases.detail: Turn real production traffic into a custom router or a specialized model you own, optimized for quality, speed and cost.

pros: Open source gateway with no markup on model calls
Covers hosted, BYOK and self-hosted models in one place
Access control and spend limits per agent
cons: You run and operate the gateway yourself
Aimed at teams that already have agent traffic to shape

name: Channels SDK
description: Channels SDK is the open-source SDK for bringing any AI agent into any chat platform: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord and Telegram, with native interactive UI. Your agent keeps its own tools, model and business logic, and Channels connects an AG-UI-compatible agent to the communication platforms your team already uses.
description_en: Channels SDK is the open-source SDK for bringing any AI agent into any chat platform: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord and Telegram, with native interactive UI. Your agent keeps its own tools, model and business logic, and Channels connects an AG-UI-compatible agent to the communication platforms your team already uses.

use_cases.title: Ship an agent to Slack or Teams
use_cases.detail: Connect an existing agent to the chat platform your team already works in without rewriting its logic.

use_cases.title: Real UI inside the channel
use_cases.detail: Give the agent native, interactive controls instead of walls of plain text.

use_cases.title: One agent, several channels
use_cases.detail: Point a single agent at Slack, Teams, Discord and Telegram at once.

pros: MIT licensed open source SDK
Your agent keeps its own model, tools and business logic
Targets Slack, Teams, Discord and Telegram
cons: Needs an AG-UI-compatible agent on your side
Developer-facing: you wire up the integration yourself

name: Wildstatic
description: Wild Static is a public AI with one shared memory. There are no separate copies: what it learns from one conversation can shape how it responds to someone else. You talk to Static in the browser and the site keeps a public log of the updates where its views changed.
description_en: Wild Static is a public AI with one shared memory. There are no separate copies: what it learns from one conversation can shape how it responds to someone else. You talk to Static in the browser and the site keeps a public log of the updates where its views changed.

use_cases.title: Talk to one shared mind
use_cases.detail: Hold a conversation with an AI whose memory is common to everyone rather than reset per user.

use_cases.title: Watch the memory change
use_cases.detail: Read the public update log that shows where and why Static changed its mind.

use_cases.title: See what others asked
use_cases.detail: Browse the public conversation stream to understand what the shared memory picked up.

pros: A genuinely different model of AI memory: one instance, not per-user copies
Public update log makes the drift visible
Nothing to install, runs in the browser
cons: Free access is limited and sometimes unavailable
Anything you type is public by design

name: Penmentor
description: Penmentor is an AI mentor that corrects your written math visually. You work by hand in xournal++, press a key, and Claude, Gemini or GPT marks your work on the screen like a teacher with coloured pens, gives hints instead of answers, and shows the idea behind the slip as a manim-style animation.
description_en: Penmentor is an AI mentor that corrects your written math visually. You work by hand in xournal++, press a key, and Claude, Gemini or GPT marks your work on the screen like a teacher with coloured pens, gives hints instead of answers, and shows the idea behind the slip as a manim-style animation.

use_cases.title: Marked where you wrote it
use_cases.detail: Get corrections drawn on the page of handwritten work instead of in a chat transcript.

use_cases.title: Hints before answers
use_cases.detail: Receive a ladder of nudges that lead you to the step rather than the final result.

use_cases.title: See the idea animated
use_cases.detail: Ask for the concept behind a mistake and watch a short generated animation of it.

pros: Works on your actual handwriting, not pasted text
Hint-first design deliberately avoids giving the answer
Runs against your own model subscription
cons: Built around xournal++ and a pen tablet
Early project with a single maintainer

name: Ambient Context
description: Ambient Context is a macOS menu bar app that writes down what you worked on during the day, in plain markdown, in a folder you own, so your AI assistant gets the context you actually saw. While it is open it reads the text of the focused window through the macOS accessibility tree and keeps a running record you can point Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client at.
description_en: Ambient Context is a macOS menu bar app that writes down what you worked on during the day, in plain markdown, in a folder you own, so your AI assistant gets the context you actually saw. While it is open it reads the text of the focused window through the macOS accessibility tree and keeps a running record you can point Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or any MCP client at.

use_cases.title: Stop re-explaining your day
use_cases.detail: Hand your assistant the reading, writing and decisions it would otherwise never see.

use_cases.title: Own the log
use_cases.detail: Keep the record as plain markdown files in a folder on your own disk.

use_cases.title: Point any MCP client at it
use_cases.detail: Give Claude Code, Cursor or Codex access to the context folder directly.

pros: Plain markdown output you control
Free and open source, shipped as a signed and notarised DMG
Works with any MCP client
cons: macOS only, version 14 or later on Apple Silicon
Relies on the macOS accessibility tree to read window text

name: Lights-on Software Factory
description: A boilerplate repository for running a lights-on software factory with Claude Code. It packages the setup used on a real product: a container sandbox that shares only the workspace directory with the host, a deterministic bash command regulator that reduces approval friction, and an orchestrator the author reports cut token spend sharply compared with running Claude workflows directly.
description_en: A boilerplate repository for running a lights-on software factory with Claude Code. It packages the setup used on a real product: a container sandbox that shares only the workspace directory with the host, a deterministic bash command regulator that reduces approval friction, and an orchestrator the author reports cut token spend sharply compared with running Claude workflows directly.

use_cases.title: Start a sandboxed project
use_cases.detail: Run Claude Code in a container that shares only your workspace directory with the host machine.

use_cases.title: Cut the approval clicks
use_cases.detail: Use a deterministic command regulator so routine shell commands stop asking for permission.

use_cases.title: Study a worked factory
use_cases.detail: Read a complete, opinionated setup rather than assembling one from blog posts.

pros: Concrete repository you can clone and run today
Isolates the agent from the rest of your machine
Doubles as a teaching example of software factory concepts
cons: Opinionated: expects you to accept its structure
Oriented to Claude Code rather than other agent CLIs

name: Chess Postmortem Skills
description: Claude Code skills that turn one of your chess games into a post-mortem you can actually read: plain-language explanations of your mistakes checked against Stockfish, an annotated PGN, an HTML viewer and a narrated video of the whole game.
description_en: Claude Code skills that turn one of your chess games into a post-mortem you can actually read: plain-language explanations of your mistakes checked against Stockfish, an annotated PGN, an HTML viewer and a narrated video of the whole game.

use_cases.title: Explain the blunder in words
use_cases.detail: Turn a PGN into annotated commentary about what actually went wrong.

use_cases.title: Check it against an engine
use_cases.detail: Cross-check the plain-language advice with a Stockfish analysis.

use_cases.title: Review on video
use_cases.detail: Render a narrated video of the game to watch instead of reading a move list.

pros: Combines engine analysis with readable explanations
Ships an HTML viewer and a narrated video, not just text
Installs as skills inside Claude Code
cons: Narrow: one game at a time, chess only
Video rendering needs extra tooling on your machine

name: SIwithin
description: SIwithin runs an agent CLI unattended on a brief, inside a fence around the folders you give it and under a dollar budget, leaving one record per run. Your home folder is refused for both reading and writing, the run cannot spend more than the dollars it was given, and every run writes a line in a ledger saying what it did.
description_en: SIwithin runs an agent CLI unattended on a brief, inside a fence around the folders you give it and under a dollar budget, leaving one record per run. Your home folder is refused for both reading and writing, the run cannot spend more than the dollars it was given, and every run writes a line in a ledger saying what it did.

use_cases.title: Let it run overnight
use_cases.detail: Hand an agent a brief and walk away without supervising every command.

use_cases.title: Cap the spend
use_cases.detail: Set a budget per run and a cap across all runs, with a timer on each one.

use_cases.title: Keep a ledger
use_cases.detail: Get one line per run recording what the agent touched and what it cost.

pros: Enforces folder boundaries with a tool rather than trust
Per-run and global budget ceilings
Metered loopback proxy so the run never holds your API key
cons: New project with a very small user base
Some agent CLIs cannot be interrupted mid-run and are refused by default

name: Aura AI Agent
description: Aura is a self-hosted, multi-user AI agent written in Go. One binary hosts the runtime, tools, CLI, Telegram gateway and an embedded web cockpit, and each person signs in to their own identity with their own memory database and workspace. It ships with temporal graph memory, scheduled jobs, MCP tools and Telegram and WhatsApp channels as a Docker Compose appliance under the MIT licence.
description_en: Aura is a self-hosted, multi-user AI agent written in Go. One binary hosts the runtime, tools, CLI, Telegram gateway and an embedded web cockpit, and each person signs in to their own identity with their own memory database and workspace. It ships with temporal graph memory, scheduled jobs, MCP tools and Telegram and WhatsApp channels as a Docker Compose appliance under the MIT licence.

use_cases.title: One appliance for a team
use_cases.detail: Run a single agent host where every person gets their own identity, memory and workspace.

use_cases.title: Give agents a schedule
use_cases.detail: Set up scheduled jobs and document retrieval alongside interactive tool use.

use_cases.title: Reach it from chat
use_cases.detail: Talk to the same agent over Telegram or WhatsApp as well as the web cockpit.

pros: Provider-neutral and self-hosted on infrastructure you control
Per-person memory separation in one deployment
Ships as a Docker Compose appliance under MIT
cons: You operate the service and pay for your own models
Early-stage: expect to read the source to configure it

name: Yana
description: Yana is a local-first, cross-platform control plane that sits between any AI model and real power over your machine. It runs, connects, orchestrates and governs agents across cloud and local model providers, with deterministic control over what an agent can access, change and execute, plus pre, post and stop hooks around every tool call.
description_en: Yana is a local-first, cross-platform control plane that sits between any AI model and real power over your machine. It runs, connects, orchestrates and governs agents across cloud and local model providers, with deterministic control over what an agent can access, change and execute, plus pre, post and stop hooks around every tool call.

use_cases.title: Give tools without giving the keys
use_cases.detail: Hand an agent real capabilities with explicit, deterministic limits on each one.

use_cases.title: One runtime, many providers
use_cases.detail: Route the same governance layer across cloud models and local ones.

use_cases.title: Gate every call
use_cases.detail: Inspect and approve tool calls before they run, and react afterwards.

pros: Clear separation between what a model proposes and what it may do
Works across several agent hosts and model providers
Hooks before, after and on stop give real oversight
cons: Young project; the surface is large and still moving
Requires comfort with a CLI control plane

name: PageIndex
description: PageIndex is a document index for vectorless, reasoning-based retrieval. Instead of chunking text into a vector database it builds a tree index and lets a model reason over it, so retrieval is context-aware and reads the way a person skims a document. It ships a Python SDK with local and cloud modes and a file-level layer for reasoning across a whole corpus.
description_en: PageIndex is a document index for vectorless, reasoning-based retrieval. Instead of chunking text into a vector database it builds a tree index and lets a model reason over it, so retrieval is context-aware and reads the way a person skims a document. It ships a Python SDK with local and cloud modes and a file-level layer for reasoning across a whole corpus.

use_cases.title: Skip the vector database
use_cases.detail: Answer questions over long PDFs by reasoning over a tree index instead of embedding chunks.

use_cases.title: Run it on your own key
use_cases.detail: Index and retrieve locally on your machine with your own LLM API key.

use_cases.title: Search a whole corpus
use_cases.detail: Use the file-level layer to reason across many documents rather than one file at a time.

pros: No chunking and no vector store to tune
Local mode keeps documents and keys on your machine
Retrieval behaves like human skimming, which is easier to debug
cons: Reasoning-based retrieval costs more tokens per query than a vector lookup
Best results depend on the model doing the reasoning

name: OpenFlow
description: OpenFlow is a visual builder for multi-agent AI workflows. You drag role cards onto a canvas, wire a pipeline such as planner, architect and coder, save it, and run it with real parallel agents. It is built on and shipped as a fork of opencode, whose headless server drives execution.
description_en: OpenFlow is a visual builder for multi-agent AI workflows. You drag role cards onto a canvas, wire a pipeline such as planner, architect and coder, save it, and run it with real parallel agents. It is built on and shipped as a fork of opencode, whose headless server drives execution.

use_cases.title: Draw the pipeline
use_cases.detail: Lay out role cards and wire them together instead of editing configuration files by hand.

use_cases.title: Run roles in parallel
use_cases.detail: Execute a planner, an architect and a coder at the same time rather than in sequence.

use_cases.title: Reuse what worked
use_cases.detail: Save a pipeline and run it again on the next project.

pros: Canvas view makes multi-agent handoffs readable
Built on an existing headless agent engine rather than a toy runtime
Pipelines are saved and reusable
cons: Fork-based approach means upgrades can lag upstream
New project, so the edges are still rough

name: DocuMemory
description: DocuMemory is a memory engine that passively distils raw AI chat sessions into permanent architecture decisions and reusable, prompt-injectable context blocks. It captures sessions from Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor and Windsurf, strips noise through subtractive distillation, then recalls and injects what matters into the next session over MCP.
description_en: DocuMemory is a memory engine that passively distils raw AI chat sessions into permanent architecture decisions and reusable, prompt-injectable context blocks. It captures sessions from Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor and Windsurf, strips noise through subtractive distillation, then recalls and injects what matters into the next session over MCP.

use_cases.title: Keep the decisions, drop the chat
use_cases.detail: Turn long sessions into architecture decision records you can read later.

use_cases.title: Start every session informed
use_cases.detail: Inject distilled context blocks into the next session automatically.

use_cases.title: Work across clients
use_cases.detail: Capture from Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, Windsurf or any MCP client.

pros: Aimed at decisions rather than raw transcript storage
MCP-native, so it drops into the clients you already use
Promises hybrid search with sub-50ms recall
cons: Hosted service with a sign-up, not something you self-host
Value depends on how much of your work happens in chat sessions

name: Nobodywho
description: Nobodywho runs AI on your own devices and servers. Its open-source inference engine ships SDKs for Rust, Python, Kotlin, Swift, Flutter, React Native and Godot, so you can run models locally with no per-token costs, no data leaving the machine and no dependency on an internet connection.
description_en: Nobodywho runs AI on your own devices and servers. Its open-source inference engine ships SDKs for Rust, Python, Kotlin, Swift, Flutter, React Native and Godot, so you can run models locally with no per-token costs, no data leaving the machine and no dependency on an internet connection.

use_cases.title: Ship inference inside an app
use_cases.detail: Embed local model calls in desktop, mobile or game builds through a language SDK.

use_cases.title: Keep sensitive data in house
use_cases.detail: Run models on-premises for data that is not allowed to leave your network.

use_cases.title: Build offline features
use_cases.detail: Offer AI features that keep working with no internet connection.

pros: No per-token costs and no vendor lock-in
Auditable engine released under an open source licence
Broad SDK coverage across languages and platforms
cons: You are responsible for model choice, hardware and updates
Enterprise support is a separate commercial offering

name: Ollaya
description: Ollaya downloads and serves open decision models on your own machine. You ask typed questions about any text or JSON, the model scores the options you define and returns the top answer with calibrated scores in milliseconds, privately and on your own hardware.
description_en: Ollaya downloads and serves open decision models on your own machine. You ask typed questions about any text or JSON, the model scores the options you define and returns the top answer with calibrated scores in milliseconds, privately and on your own hardware.

use_cases.title: Classify support mail
use_cases.detail: Score incoming messages for intent, urgency and tone without sending them anywhere.

use_cases.title: Get typed answers
use_cases.detail: Ask structured questions with fixed options instead of parsing free-form text.

use_cases.title: Run it in a pipeline
use_cases.detail: Call the CLI from shell scripts and batch jobs as a scoring step.

pros: Typed, calibrated output instead of prose you have to parse
Runs locally with no network dependency
Open source and independent of the vendors it borrows ideas from
cons: Limited to the decision models in its catalogue
Local inference speed depends on your hardware

name: Cloudflare cf CLI
description: cf is Cloudflare agentic CLI for the whole Cloudflare API. Commands are discoverable through built-in search and steering so an agent can find the command it needs, JSON is the default interface, pretty printed for humans and condensed for agents to save context, and cloudflare.config.ts becomes the single configuration format for the platform.
description_en: cf is Cloudflare agentic CLI for the whole Cloudflare API. Commands are discoverable through built-in search and steering so an agent can find the command it needs, JSON is the default interface, pretty printed for humans and condensed for agents to save context, and cloudflare.config.ts becomes the single configuration format for the platform.

use_cases.title: Let an agent drive your account
use_cases.detail: Expose the whole Cloudflare API to an agent through commands it can discover itself.

use_cases.title: Save context on output
use_cases.detail: Get condensed JSON for agents and readable output for humans from the same commands.

use_cases.title: Unify configuration
use_cases.detail: Move to a single cloudflare.config.ts instead of scattered per-service config.

pros: Built for agents first, with search and steering baked in
JSON-native interface reduces parsing glue code
Official Cloudflare project covering the full API
cons: Only useful if you already run on Cloudflare
Replaces habits built around the older Wrangler workflow

name: Imp
description: Imp is a full port of DSPy to the BEAM. You describe what each language-model step takes and returns, choose how it thinks, and let an optimizer improve the program against examples of what good looks like, giving you signatures, modules, optimizers, agent loops and retrieval with the concurrency and reliability of OTP.
description_en: Imp is a full port of DSPy to the BEAM. You describe what each language-model step takes and returns, choose how it thinks, and let an optimizer improve the program against examples of what good looks like, giving you signatures, modules, optimizers, agent loops and retrieval with the concurrency and reliability of OTP.

use_cases.title: Write declarative LM programs
use_cases.detail: Describe inputs and outputs per step rather than hand-writing prompts.

use_cases.title: Optimize against examples
use_cases.detail: Let an optimizer tune the program using examples of good output.

use_cases.title: Run it on OTP
use_cases.detail: Get agent loops and retrieval supervised by the BEAM runtime.

pros: Brings the DSPy programming model to Elixir and Erlang teams
Concurrency and supervision come from OTP rather than bolted-on plumbing
Optimizers mean less manual prompt tuning
cons: Requires Elixir and willingness to think in signatures
Smaller ecosystem than the Python original

name: Konnect
description: Konnect brings AI-assisted PCB design to KiCad 10. It is a native KiCad plugin, a single Rust binary, that exposes hundreds of schematic, layout, routing, placement, design-review and manufacturing tools to Claude or the model of your choice over the Model Context Protocol, grouped into on-demand toolsets.
description_en: Konnect brings AI-assisted PCB design to KiCad 10. It is a native KiCad plugin, a single Rust binary, that exposes hundreds of schematic, layout, routing, placement, design-review and manufacturing tools to Claude or the model of your choice over the Model Context Protocol, grouped into on-demand toolsets.

use_cases.title: Capture a schematic by asking
use_cases.detail: Have an assistant place parts and wire a schematic from a description.

use_cases.title: Audit before fabrication
use_cases.detail: Run ERC, DRC and design-review checks through the same conversational interface.

use_cases.title: Search parts in context
use_cases.detail: Look up distributor parts and reference circuits without leaving KiCad.

pros: Deep KiCad coverage rather than a thin wrapper
Toolsets load on demand so the model context stays manageable
Model-agnostic over MCP
cons: Beta release tied to KiCad 10
Hardware work still needs a human to sanity-check the result

name: JetBrains Air
description: JetBrains Air is one system for building software with agents. It works with the agents you already use, Claude Agent, Codex, Junie, Copilot, OpenCode and anything you can connect over ACP, and gives you tasks, automations and projects you can drive from JetBrains IDEs, the web, the CLI or a phone.
description_en: JetBrains Air is one system for building software with agents. It works with the agents you already use, Claude Agent, Codex, Junie, Copilot, OpenCode and anything you can connect over ACP, and gives you tasks, automations and projects you can drive from JetBrains IDEs, the web, the CLI or a phone.

use_cases.title: Keep your existing agent
use_cases.detail: Bring Claude Agent, Codex, Junie, Copilot or OpenCode into one task system.

use_cases.title: Automate the chores
use_cases.detail: Set up automations such as rebasing a branch or updating agent instructions on merge.

use_cases.title: Work from anywhere
use_cases.detail: Drive the same projects from an IDE, a browser, a terminal or mobile.

pros: Agent-agnostic through the ACP protocol
Spans IDE, web, CLI and mobile rather than one surface
Tasks, automations and projects share one model
cons: Commercial product with a credit-based pricing model
Most valuable if you already live in JetBrains tooling

name: PatchWave
description: PatchWave is a GitHub app that automatically analyzes, fixes and merges your Dependabot pull requests. Its agent checks each dependency update against your code and repairs what breaks, so dependency bumps stop piling up in the review queue.
description_en: PatchWave is a GitHub app that automatically analyzes, fixes and merges your Dependabot pull requests. Its agent checks each dependency update against your code and repairs what breaks, so dependency bumps stop piling up in the review queue.

use_cases.title: Clear the PR backlog
use_cases.detail: Let an agent work the queue of dependency bumps instead of a human.

use_cases.title: Fix what the bump broke
use_cases.detail: Check the update against your code and repair the fallout before merging.

use_cases.title: Keep the audit trail
use_cases.detail: Every merge arrives as a normal pull request with its analysis attached.

pros: Attacks a queue almost every team has given up on
Free tier covers a monthly allowance of merged PRs
Installs as a GitHub app with no pipeline rewrite
cons: Merging automatically needs trust in the analysis
Focused on Dependabot rather than other update sources

name: MirrorMD
description: MirrorMD is a facial analysis built by a cosmetic surgeon. It measures your face the way a consultation does and tells you which treatments may suit you, which would waste your money and which could harm you, before you spend anything on them.
description_en: MirrorMD is a facial analysis built by a cosmetic surgeon. It measures your face the way a consultation does and tells you which treatments may suit you, which would waste your money and which could harm you, before you spend anything on them.

use_cases.title: Screen the treatment first
use_cases.detail: Get an opinion on whether a procedure suits your face before booking it.

use_cases.title: Avoid the wasted spend
use_cases.detail: Find out which popular treatments would do nothing for you.

use_cases.title: Hear the risks
use_cases.detail: Learn which options carry harm rather than benefit in your case.

pros: Written by a practising cosmetic surgeon rather than a generic beauty quiz
Explicitly willing to say a treatment is a bad idea
Positioned before you spend money, not after
cons: Paid analysis, not a free checker
Advice from a tool is not a substitute for an in-person examination

name: Worklicant
description: Worklicant is a tech hiring platform where AI reads every resume and ranks your applicants. You share one apply link, it scores each applicant against the job, hides spam and fake resumes, and auto-rejects people who fail your deal-breaker, while candidates book their own interviews.
description_en: Worklicant is a tech hiring platform where AI reads every resume and ranks your applicants. You share one apply link, it scores each applicant against the job, hides spam and fake resumes, and auto-rejects people who fail your deal-breaker, while candidates book their own interviews.

use_cases.title: Post once, share everywhere
use_cases.detail: Put a single apply link on LinkedIn, job boards and your careers page.

use_cases.title: Rank by fit
use_cases.detail: See applicants sorted by a score against the role instead of arrival order.

use_cases.title: Filter the noise
use_cases.detail: Hide spam, fake resumes and anyone who fails a deal-breaker you set.

pros: Pay per vacancy rather than a monthly seat subscription
Unlimited team members on a posting
Candidates self-schedule interviews
cons: Newest entrant in a crowded applicant-tracking field
Automated rejection needs care to avoid filtering out good candidates

name: Tori
description: Tori is an AI support agent for customer success teams, built on TalkJS messaging infrastructure. It learns your product from the help docs, product pages and company knowledge you already have, then answers even complex customer questions through a UI you can customize, handing off to a human with full context when a customer needs one.
description_en: Tori is an AI support agent for customer success teams, built on TalkJS messaging infrastructure. It learns your product from the help docs, product pages and company knowledge you already have, then answers even complex customer questions through a UI you can customize, handing off to a human with full context when a customer needs one.

use_cases.title: Answer from what you published
use_cases.detail: Point it at your URL and let it answer from your own documentation.

use_cases.title: Keep your branding
use_cases.detail: Customize the support UI instead of embedding someone else widget.

use_cases.title: Escalate cleanly
use_cases.detail: Hand a conversation to a human with the history attached.

pros: Built on production messaging infrastructure with real delivery and history
Setup starts from a URL rather than a data migration
Customizable front end
cons: Best for teams whose answers already exist in documentation
Pricing is not published up front

name: Invofox
description: Invofox turns invoices, payslips, contracts and other documents into structured JSON through one API. You pay only for pages it extracts correctly, and the extraction keeps learning from corrections you make.
description_en: Invofox turns invoices, payslips, contracts and other documents into structured JSON through one API. You pay only for pages it extracts correctly, and the extraction keeps learning from corrections you make.

use_cases.title: Replace the template zoo
use_cases.detail: Extract fields from any document layout through one endpoint.

use_cases.title: Pay for correct pages
use_cases.detail: Get billed only on pages the extraction got right.

use_cases.title: Improve over time
use_cases.detail: Feed corrections back so recurring layouts get cleaner.

pros: Single API across invoices, payslips and contracts
Billing tied to correct extractions rather than raw volume
Continuous learning from corrections
cons: Commercial API, so documents leave your infrastructure
Correct-page billing model is unusual and worth reading carefully

name: Layout
description: Layout lets you order food from any restaurant using AI. It connects Claude and ChatGPT to real ordering, so your assistant can place the order end to end, and it exposes a developer console and merchant dashboard for building on top of the same rails.
description_en: Layout lets you order food from any restaurant using AI. It connects Claude and ChatGPT to real ordering, so your assistant can place the order end to end, and it exposes a developer console and merchant dashboard for building on top of the same rails.

use_cases.title: Order through your assistant
use_cases.detail: Ask Claude or ChatGPT to place a real food order rather than just find a restaurant.

use_cases.title: Connect a platform
use_cases.detail: Add a connector so an agent can transact on an existing delivery service.

use_cases.title: Build on the rails
use_cases.detail: Use the developer console to integrate ordering into your own product.

pros: One of the first attempts at real agent-side commerce rather than recommendations
Has both developer and merchant sides from the start
Explicit model of delegated spending authority
cons: Availability depends on participating merchants
Handing spending authority to an agent needs trust in the limits you set

name: Jurl
description: Jurl is curl for pages you want read rather than fetched. You tell it what you want from a URL and it scrapes with intent, returning only what you asked for word for word, and following links when the answer sits several pages away.
description_en: Jurl is curl for pages you want read rather than fetched. You tell it what you want from a URL and it scrapes with intent, returning only what you asked for word for word, and following links when the answer sits several pages away.

use_cases.title: Ask instead of grep
use_cases.detail: Describe the value you want and get it back rather than a document to parse.

use_cases.title: Follow the trail
use_cases.detail: Let it walk links when the fact you need is not on the first page.

use_cases.title: Keep it scriptable
use_cases.detail: Use it as a command line step in shell pipelines and agent tools.

pros: Returns the answer, not the page
Follows links when the target is pages away
Fits naturally into a terminal workflow
cons: Depends on a model call per query
Accuracy on long trails still needs a human eye

name: AgentSocialX
description: AgentSocialX is a Second Brain Network. You start your second brain from LinkedIn and X, then use the network to get answers and opinions from other peoples second brains and to set up one-on-ones. The pitch is that your AI keeps learning from the network while your own thinking gets found by the right mind.
description_en: AgentSocialX is a Second Brain Network. You start your second brain from LinkedIn and X, then use the network to get answers and opinions from other peoples second brains and to set up one-on-ones. The pitch is that your AI keeps learning from the network while your own thinking gets found by the right mind.

use_cases.title: Seed it from your profiles
use_cases.detail: Build a second brain starting from what you already posted on LinkedIn and X.

use_cases.title: Ask people, not feeds
use_cases.detail: Get answers and opinions from other members second brains.

use_cases.title: Turn matches into calls
use_cases.detail: Move from a shared interest to a one-on-one conversation.

pros: Focuses on connecting people through their notes rather than follower counts
Imports from profiles you already have
Public counters make network activity visible
cons: Value depends on who else joins
Handing your notes to a network means thinking about what you publish there

name: Plannotator
description: Plannotator is free, open-source review tooling for Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Pi and Droid. You review an agent plan before it executes, annotate agent-written code in a full diff viewer, and send structured feedback straight back to the agent, all running locally. Its Inbox collects your agents questions, plans and reviews in one window.
description_en: Plannotator is free, open-source review tooling for Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Pi and Droid. You review an agent plan before it executes, annotate agent-written code in a full diff viewer, and send structured feedback straight back to the agent, all running locally. Its Inbox collects your agents questions, plans and reviews in one window.

use_cases.title: Read the plan first
use_cases.detail: Inspect and edit what an agent intends to do before it touches the repository.

use_cases.title: Annotate the diff
use_cases.detail: Comment on agent-written code in a viewer rather than in a chat log.

use_cases.title: Answer from one window
use_cases.detail: Use the Inbox to handle questions, plans and reviews from several agents.

pros: Free and open source, running locally rather than as a hosted service
Works across several agent CLIs instead of one
Feedback goes back to the agent in structured form
cons: Adds a deliberate pause to agent workflows
Local-only means no shared review with a team by default

name: Daydream Studio
description: Daydream Studio is a hybrid recording studio in the browser for crafting and producing music. You generate or record a part, add live session-player tracks over it, and reshape the parts as they play. The page also exposes a scriptable interface so agents can drive the studio directly.
description_en: Daydream Studio is a hybrid recording studio in the browser for crafting and producing music. You generate or record a part, add live session-player tracks over it, and reshape the parts as they play. The page also exposes a scriptable interface so agents can drive the studio directly.

use_cases.title: Build a track in the browser
use_cases.detail: Generate or record a part without installing a DAW.

use_cases.title: Add real players
use_cases.detail: Layer live session-player tracks over what you generated.

use_cases.title: Let an agent drive it
use_cases.detail: Script the studio through its exposed interface for agent-driven sessions.

pros: Combines generated parts with human session playing
Runs in a browser tab with no install
Scriptable surface makes it usable by agents
cons: Best on a desktop rather than a phone
Output quality still depends on your own ear and editing

name: Reduck
description: Reduck is an MCP server that lets your agent create and run reusable automation scripts for the web. Instead of reasoning through every click, the agent writes or reuses a script that returns the same structured output each time, runs in your own Chrome, and burns no tokens while it executes.
description_en: Reduck is an MCP server that lets your agent create and run reusable automation scripts for the web. Instead of reasoning through every click, the agent writes or reuses a script that returns the same structured output each time, runs in your own Chrome, and burns no tokens while it executes.

use_cases.title: Make the web deterministic
use_cases.detail: Turn a flaky click-by-click task into a script with a clear contract.

use_cases.title: Stop paying per step
use_cases.detail: Run scripts that cost no tokens and do not grow the context window.

use_cases.title: Reuse across sites
use_cases.detail: Keep a library of scripts the agent can call on any website.

pros: Scripts return consistent structured output instead of varying per run
Runs in your own Chrome with your own logged-in sessions
Ships ready-made scripts for common sites
cons: Someone still has to write or fix the script when a site changes
Hosted MCP service rather than a local-only tool

name: Datastory
description: Datastory is a no-code platform for data storytellers. You upload your own data or search a curated catalog of open datasets, then build interactive charts, websites and reports with its Studio, CMS and AI features.
description_en: Datastory is a no-code platform for data storytellers. You upload your own data or search a curated catalog of open datasets, then build interactive charts, websites and reports with its Studio, CMS and AI features.

use_cases.title: Start from your own file
use_cases.detail: Upload a spreadsheet and turn it into an interactive chart or report.

use_cases.title: Or start from open data
use_cases.detail: Search a catalog of curated open datasets instead of sourcing your own.

use_cases.title: Publish the result
use_cases.detail: Use the CMS to turn charts into a website rather than a static image.

pros: No-code path from raw data to a published story
Bundles a catalog of open datasets to start from
Studio, CMS and AI features in one product
cons: Aimed at storytellers rather than analysts needing deep statistics
Commercial platform with tiered plans

name: Privatemode
description: Privatemode is a confidential AI service that protects your data end to end. Using confidential computing, it encrypts your data before it leaves your device and keeps it protected even while the model is processing it, including inside Excel, Word and PowerPoint.
description_en: Privatemode is a confidential AI service that protects your data end to end. Using confidential computing, it encrypts your data before it leaves your device and keeps it protected even while the model is processing it, including inside Excel, Word and PowerPoint.

use_cases.title: Use AI on sensitive files
use_cases.detail: Work with documents that are not allowed to be exposed to a model provider.

use_cases.title: Keep Office in the loop
use_cases.detail: Get AI help inside Excel, Word and PowerPoint with the same protection.

use_cases.title: Prove it technically
use_cases.detail: Rely on confidential computing isolation rather than a contractual promise.

pros: Encryption holds during processing, not only in transit
Extends to the Office tools people actually work in
Aimed at regulated and security-conscious teams
cons: Commercial service you have to evaluate and trust
Protection depends on the attestation model behind it

name: Feyn
description: Feyn is a platform for training custom models on your own data. It keeps learning in production, serves faster and cheaper inference, and lets you own the weights. Its open-source releases include MultiMatte and FeyNoBg, models for promptable image background removal.
description_en: Feyn is a platform for training custom models on your own data. It keeps learning in production, serves faster and cheaper inference, and lets you own the weights. Its open-source releases include MultiMatte and FeyNoBg, models for promptable image background removal.

use_cases.title: Train on your own examples
use_cases.detail: Build a model around your data instead of prompting a general one.

use_cases.title: Keep improving after launch
use_cases.detail: Let the model keep learning once it is in production.

use_cases.title: Cut the background
use_cases.detail: Use its open matting models for promptable image background removal.

pros: You own the weights rather than renting a behaviour
Production learning loop rather than a one-off fine-tune
Open source model releases alongside the platform
cons: Platform is commercially oriented; pricing is not published
Training and serving your own models needs ML ops maturity
